# konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule (Resource)

AICostBudgetNotificationRule Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule" "my_aicostbudgetnotificationrule" {
  budget_id = "fc085564-33b2-47d5-9bc0-a0a7d4deb834"
  channels = [
    {
      id = "8c219a7a-8116-4d1a-a1d5-98945f0141e4"
    }
  ]
  message = {
    body    = "...my_body..."
    subject = "...my_subject..."
  }
  thresholds = [
    {
      percent = 704
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `budget_id` (String) The `id` of the budget. Requires replacement if changed.
- `thresholds` (Attributes Set) The shares of the limit at which the rule fires. Each threshold fires at most once per budget window, derived budget, and limit, and changing the limit lets the thresholds fire again.

1 to 10 thresholds, each with a different `percent`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--thresholds))

### Optional

- `channels` (Attributes Set) The channels that receive the rule's alerts.

At most 10 channels, each listed once. Reads return them ordered by channel name. Defaults to `[]`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--channels))
- `message` (Attributes) The wording of the rule's alerts on every channel, or `null` for the built-in wording.

`subject` and `body` can contain placeholders, such as `{{budget.name}}`. A placeholder is `{{`, optional whitespace, a name from the list below, optional whitespace, and `}}`. There's no escaping, and a lone `}}` is text. Each alert fills the placeholders with its own values. Amounts appear in US dollars, such as `$4,125.50`.

- `{{budget.name}}`: the budget's name.
- `{{budget.url}}`: a link to the budget in Konnect.
- `{{threshold}}`: the threshold that was crossed, such as `80%`.
- `{{limit}}`: the limit that spend is measured against. With `each`, the limit of one derived budget.
- `{{spend}}`: the spend so far in the budget window.
- `{{percent}}`: the spend as a share of the limit, such as `82.51%`.
- `{{remaining}}`: what is left of the limit, never below `$0.00`.
- `{{projected}}`: where spend ends the budget window at the current pace, as an amount and a share of the limit.
- `{{period}}`: the budget window, in the time zone of its anchor.
- `{{period.start}}`: when the budget window started.
- `{{period.end}}`: when the budget window ends and the budget resets.
- `{{period.remaining}}`: how long is left in the budget window when the alert is sent, in its largest whole unit, such as `8 days` or `12 minutes`. Under a minute, it's `less than a minute`, and after the window ends, `no time`.
- `{{entity.field}}`: the `each` field as a noun, such as `group`, `user` for `subject`, or `env tag` for `tags.env`.
- `{{entity.value}}`: the value whose derived budget crossed the threshold. A Kong Identity principal or a consumer shows as its display name when the service can resolve it. Any other value shows as it is.

`{{entity.field}}` and `{{entity.value}}` work only on a budget with `each`. Defaults to `null`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--message))

### Read-Only

- `budget` (Attributes) The budget the rule belongs to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--budget))
- `created_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity creation date.
- `updated_at` (String) An ISO-8601 timestamp representation of entity update date.

Optional:

1 to 1000.
Not Null

Optional:

### Nested Schema for `message`

Required:

- `body` (String) The text of the rule's alerts, as plain text that can contain placeholders such as `{{budget.name}}`. Blank lines separate paragraphs.

1 to 2000 characters after the server removes leading and trailing whitespace.
- `subject` (String) The subject line of the rule's alerts, as plain text that can contain placeholders such as `{{budget.name}}`.

A single line of 1 to 200 characters after the server removes leading and trailing whitespace.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule.my_konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule
  id = "..."
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule.my_konnect_ai_cost_budget_notification_rule "..."
```
